# # This is a Shiny web application. You can run the application by clicking # the 'Run App' button above. # # Find out more about building applications with Shiny here: # # https://shiny.posit.co/ # #install.packages("shinylive") #install.packages("httpuv") #install.packages("openssl") library(shiny) library(shinyWidgets) library(ggplot2) library(dplyr) library(plotly) library(leaflet) library(ggsignif) # Check that app.R is in your current directory: #file.exists("app.R") # If TRUE, export using the current directory: #shinylive::export(appdir = ".", destdir = "docs") #install.packages("S7", repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org") #unlink(rappdirs::user_cache_dir("shinylive"), recursive = TRUE) #shinylive::export(appdir = "Litterfall_Project", destdir = "docs") #library(rsconnect) # ------------------------------------------------------------------------- # 1. DATA IMPLEMENTATION (Your real comprehensive statistical dataset) # ------------------------------------------------------------------------- # Put this at the top of Litterfall_Project/app.R data_file <- if (file.exists("Data/all_days.csv")) { "Data/all_days.csv" } else if (file.exists("Litterfall_Project/Data/all_days.csv")) { "Litterfall_Project/Data/all_days.csv" } else { stop("all_days.csv not found") } alldays <- read.csv(data_file) collar_stats <- data.frame( Collar = c("L1", "L2", "L3", "L4", "M1", "M2", "M3", "M4", "U1", "U2", "U3", "U4"), Treatment = c("senesced", "green", "soil", "control", "senesced", "green", "soil", "control", "senesced", "green", "soil", "control"), Slope = c("lower", "lower", "lower", "lower", "middle", "middle", "middle", "middle", "upper", "upper", "upper", "upper"), Mean_CO2Flux = c(4.406564, 4.435556, 3.755266, 4.161547, 5.652713, 4.580049, 3.471339, 4.223396, 4.142587, 2.750622, 2.231453, 1.250909), SD_CO2Flux = c(0.7315073, 0.7258934, 1.6797948, 0.8705890, 2.1114814, 0.9445531, 0.5941946, 1.1611924, 1.0614012, 0.8066849, 0.5866173, 0.3360746), Mean_CH4Flux = c(-0.47753556, -0.28314889, -0.36127444, -0.25832889, -1.10237889, -0.63362222, -0.65553778, -0.45520778, -0.55305000, -0.16641778, -0.32511111, -0.03839111), SD_CH4Flux = c(0.12553209, 0.26593712, 0.19169599, 0.11218048, 0.23386749, 0.37215248, 0.18928341, 0.19366809, 0.12740937, 0.06118727, 0.15831931, 0.06011285), Mean_SM = c(0.2711633, 0.2871600, 0.3920967, 0.3424500, 0.2215378, 0.2780267, 0.2441289, 0.3306978, 0.2930944, 0.4712033, 0.2799911, 0.4030022), SD_SM = c(0.08242494, 0.11409810, 0.09880072, 0.10384049, 0.06117822, 0.08074628, 0.09093912, 0.13787704, 0.07298433, 0.07527976, 0.05805731, 0.1349452), Mean_ST = c(26.48737, 26.68889, 26.56667, 26.62980, 26.92222, 26.98889, 27.00303, 26.83333, 26.85051, 26.97778, 27.03081, 26.88889), SD_ST = c(0.9915341, 0.7623064, 0.7842194, 0.7892979, 0.6476453, 0.5060742, 0.4720271, 1.0198039, 0.8034020, 0.4352522, 0.4088748, 0.5418589) ) # Significance annotations for CO2 control_vs_green_sig_co2 <- "*" control_vs_senesced_sig_co2 <- "***" # Significance annotations for CH4 (Adjust as needed based on your ANOVA/t-test results) control_vs_green_sig_ch4 <- "*" control_vs_senesced_sig_ch4 <- "***" control_vs_soil_sig_ch4 <- "***" # Simulated raw 'alldays' dataset featuring matching columns # (In your local script, your loaded 'alldays' dataset will take its place) timepoints_list <- c("pretreatment", "day1", "day2", "day3", "day4", "day5", "day6", "day7", "day8") alldays$Timepoint <- factor(alldays$Timepoint, levels = timepoints_list) alldays <- data.frame( Collar = rep(collar_stats$Collar, each = 9), Timepoint = rep(timepoints_list, times = 12), Treatment = rep(collar_stats$Treatment, each = 9), Slope = rep(collar_stats$Slope, each = 9), CO2Flux = rnorm(108, mean = 4, sd = 1.2), CH4Flux = rnorm(108, mean = -0.4, sd = 0.2), SoilMoisture = runif(108, min = 0.1, max = 0.5), SoilTemp = runif(108, min = 15, max = 30) ) # Add spatial coordinates to your existing collar_stats data frame collar_stats$lat <- c( # Lower Slope (L1-L4) 18.3150, 18.3151, 18.3152, 18.3153, # Middle Slope (M1-M4) 18.3160, 18.3161, 18.3162, 18.3163, # Upper Slope (U1-U4) 18.3170, 18.3171, 18.3172, 18.3173 ) collar_stats$lng <- c( # Lower Slope -65.7960, -65.7958, -65.7956, -65.7954, # Middle Slope -65.7950, -65.7948, -65.7946, -65.7944, # Upper Slope -65.7940, -65.7938, -65.7936, -65.7934 ) # ------------------------------------------------------------------------- # 2. USER INTERFACE (UI) # ------------------------------------------------------------------------- ui <- fluidPage( titlePanel("Litterfall Experiment: Master Dashboard"), tabsetPanel( # NEW TAB 1: Project Introduction & Photo tabPanel("Overview", # 1. Title Row (Spans the full 12 units) fluidRow( column(12, h2("Implications of Hurricane and Drought Disturbance in El Yunque National Forest: Comparison between CO2 and CH4 Fluxes in Green vs. Senesced Litterfall"), hr() ) ), # 2. Content Row (Split into Left and Right) fluidRow( # LEFT COLUMN: Text description (8 units wide) column(12, h4("Purpose"), p("When I first began this research project, I was focused on gaining hands-on experience out in the field. I learned a lot about what it meant to be scientist, a collaborator, and a student. I wanted to ensure that my research acknowledged Puerto Rico, their history, and their people. Science is meant to be shared and communicated and in unique ways. Accessibily to research can be very limited, especially to underrepresented communities. The purpose of this Shiny App is to display my findings for the public while practicing my data science skills. I want to ensure that this site is accessible for all communities. As I progress in my academic career, I want to study science communication and how we can better in across all societies. Within this Shiny App, you can find my results, my experimental methods, and why it is important to study troical rainforests. "), ), column(12, h4("Background"), p("Climate change is leading to an increase in both frequency and severity of hurricanes and droughts in many parts of the globe. It remains unclear how those shifting disturbance patterns might impact ecosystems. Puerto Rico has experienced both historically severe droughts and hurricanes. Hurricane Maria was a catastrophic event that took a toll on many families and economically impacted citizens negatively. Puerto Rico also experienced a severe drought leaving many populations without water and impacting the agriculture industry. As larger hurricanes and severe droughts become more common in the Caribbean, it will be crucial to study the long-term effects on the carbon storage of the region’s tropical rainforests."), ), ), # A row containing 6 side-by-side pictures # A row containing 6 photos touching seamlessly with no spaces fluidRow( # Custom CSS to remove column padding and force images to span 100% width tags$head( tags$style(HTML(" .no-padding > [class*='col-'] { padding-left: 0 !important; padding-right: 0 !important; } .no-padding img { width: 100%; aspect-ratio: 1 / 1 !important; /* Enforces strict 1:1 square ratio */ object-fit: cover !important; /* Prevents stretching/distortion */ display: block !important; /* Eliminates whitespace gap */ } ")) ), # Wrapper container using the 'no-padding' class div(class = "no-padding", column(2, img(src = "val_and_natalie.jpg")), column(2, img(src = "senesced.jpg")), column(2, img(src = "val_and_sc.jpg")), column(2, img(src = "trace.jpg")), column(2, img(src = "smart_chamber_wifi.jpg")), column(2, img(src = "fieldstation.jpg")) ) ) ), #possible panel 2 with collar map tabPanel("Methodology", fluidRow( column(12, h4("Experimental Design"), p("Our study was conducted in El Yunque National Forest in Puerto Rico in collaboration with TRACE. Their ongoing project oversees about 3000 sq miles, where there are 12 soil collars placed outside their warming and control plots. There are 4 soil collars at 3 slope levels: lower, mid, and upper. At each level, the four soil collars represent a treatment. The four treatments are: senesced leaves, green leaves, bare soil, and a control group [collar left untouched]. We obtained the senesced and green leaves from one leaf species, Guarea guidonia. We ensured that there were two layers of leaves for each treatment, by standardizing the weight between wet and dry leaves."), ), fluidRow( column(12, h3("Spatial Distribution of Soil Collars"), p("This is a map of where the soil collars were located along each slope. Coordinates were found through a mix of GPS and photos taken on iPhone."), leafletOutput("collar_map", height = "550px") ) ) ), tabsetPanel( # DATA TAB 1: Collar Profile Card tabPanel("Collar Stats", sidebarLayout( sidebarPanel( h3("Collar Selector"), p("Select any collar ID to see its traits and real gas/moisture summary metrics."), selectInput("selected_collar", "Select Collar ID:", choices = as.list(collar_stats$Collar)) ), mainPanel( h2(uiOutput("collar_title")), hr(), fluidRow( column(6, wellPanel( h4("Physical Attributes"), htmlOutput("collar_metadata") ) ), column(6, wellPanel( h4("Summary Statistics"), htmlOutput("collar_gas_stats") ) ) ) ) ) ) ) ), # DATA TAB 2: Dynamic Treatment Selector (Bar Graphs) tabPanel("Figures of Treatments", sidebarLayout( sidebarPanel( h3("Greenhouse Gas Flux Selector"), p("Select a gas metric to view the fluxes at different slope levels and overall treatment significance tests."), radioButtons("metric", "Choose Gas Metric:", choices = list("Carbon Dioxide (CO2)" = "CO2", "Methane (CH4)" = "CH4")) ), mainPanel( # --- Plot 1: Collar & Slope Distributions --- plotlyOutput("summary_bar_chart"), wellPanel( h5(strong("Figure 1: Mean CO2 and CH4 Across Soil Collars by Litter Treatment and Slope Position")), p("This is an interactive graph! Hover over the bar graph and error bars to view the values. The figure shows the the mean gas flux of CO2 and CH4 across individual soil collars grouped by treatment and broken down by slope position (Lower [L], Middle [M], and Upper [U]).") ), hr(), # --- Plot 2: Treatment Significance --- plotOutput("treatment_signif_chart"), wellPanel( h5(strong("Figure 2 Explanation: Overall Treatment Comparisons")), p("This graph compares pooled treatment averages against one another. Brackets denote pairwise statistical comparisons, where asterisks indicate significant differences (e.g., * p < 0.05, *** p < 0.001) between treatment groups.") ) ) ) ), # DATA TAB 3: Timeline Explorer ($2 \times 2$ Grid Dashboard) # DATA TAB 3: Longitudinal Timeline Explorer (Concept 1) tabPanel("Timeline Explorer", sidebarLayout( sidebarPanel( h3("Timeline Controls"), p("Examine continuous trends across sampling days and compare gas fluxes directly with microclimate dynamics."), # 1. Choose Gas Flux radioButtons("timeline_gas", "Select Gas Flux Metric:", choices = list("Carbon Dioxide (CO2)" = "CO2Flux", "Methane (CH4)" = "CH4Flux"), selected = "CO2Flux"), hr(), # 2. Filter by Collars selectizeInput( inputId = "selected_timeline_collars", label = "Choose Collars to Display:", choices = list( "Lower Slope" = c("L1", "L2", "L3", "L4"), "Middle Slope" = c("M1", "M2", "M3", "M4"), "Upper Slope" = c("U1", "U2", "U3", "U4") ), selected = c("L1", "M1", "U1"), multiple = TRUE, options = list( placeholder = "Click to select collars...", plugins = list("remove_button") ) ) ), mainPanel( # Top Plot: Gas Flux Trajectory plotOutput("timeline_gas_plot", height = "320px"), # Bottom Plot: Abiotic Factors (Soil Moisture & Temperature) plotOutput("timeline_abiotic_plot", height = "320px"), # Explanatory panel wellPanel( h5(strong("Comparing Fluxes to Abiotic Drivers Over Time")), p("The upper plot highlights greenhouse gas dynamics over the 8-day observation window, while the lower plot tracks synchronous changes in soil moisture and temperature. Aligning them along the same timeline allows direct visual inspection of whether gas pulses corresponded to wetting events or warming periods.") ) ) ) ), # TAB 4: Conclusion & Acknowledgments tabPanel("Conclusion", fluidRow( column(12, h2("Conclusion"), hr(), p("Our findings show that litterfall with green and senesced litterfall do have significantly higher CO2 and lower CH4 flux levels as compared to the control group. For CH4 fluxes specifically, all treatments (senesced, green, and soil) were all significantly lower than the control group. CO2 fluxes did not show a statistical significance between soil treatment and the control group. This overall supports our research question how hurricanes and droughts represented through green and senesced leaves will have greater CO2 and CH4 intake and release. "), h4(strong("Why This Matters")), p("Tropical forests are known as large carbon sinks. It is important to explore their dynamics at different scales to better understand how they will respond to progressing climate change. That is why I focused on the ground floor, focusing on soil microclimate and how fallen leaves will slowly affect CO2 and CH4 fluxes. This research tells how litter from both senesced and green leaves will drive higher CO2 emissions back into the atmosphere, contributing to a positive feedback loop that accelerates climate change. Along with the data that I found, it is just as important to communicate my findings in ways that reach audiences outside of the academic world. Promoting science communication, open science, and accessibility is hard to navigate for certain communities. By creating this interactive webpage through Shiny, I hope to reach people who have interests in science who may not necessarily have the resources or opportunities to learn more about climate change."), hr(), h2("Acknowledgments"), p("I would like to thank the team at TRACE (Tropical Responses to Altered Climate Experiment) including Tatiana Barreto-Vélez, Laura Rubio-Lebrón, Deyaneira Ortiz-Iglesias, and Rachel Cruz-Pérez. Thank you to the O’Connell Lab at Chapman University and Gabriele Larocca Conte. Most importantly, I would like to thank my fellow peers and interns: Natalie Peterson-Hunt, Sofia Brege, Daliz Casablanca, and Katia Hnatiw. This project would not have been possible without everyone’s support, collaboration, and mentorship."), br() ) ), # Seamless photo strip matching the Overview page styling fluidRow( div(class = "no-padding", column(2, img(src = "christine_team.jpg")), column(2, img(src = "val_and_nat_in_field.jpg")), column(2, img(src = "trace_team1.jpg")), column(2, img(src = "sofianatval.jpg")), column(2, img(src = "trace_team2.png")), column(2, img(src = "val_field_dirty.jpg")) ) ), br() ) ) # End of tabsetPanel ) # ------------------------------------------------------------------------- # 3. SERVER LOGIC # ------------------------------------------------------------------------- server <- function(input, output, session) { #the possible panel 2 output$collar_map <- renderLeaflet({ # Create HTML content for the pop-up boxes when a marker is clicked popup_info <- paste0( "Collar ID: ", collar_stats$Collar, "
", "Slope Position: ", tools::toTitleCase(collar_stats$Slope), "
", "Treatment: ", tools::toTitleCase(collar_stats$Treatment), "
", "Mean CO₂ Flux: ", round(collar_stats$Mean_CO2Flux, 2), " μmol/m²/s
", "Mean CH₄ Flux: ", round(collar_stats$Mean_CH4Flux, 2), " nmol/m²/s" ) leaflet(collar_stats) %>% # Adds a realistic satellite imagery basemap addProviderTiles(providers$Esri.WorldImagery) %>% # Focus the view over the research site in Puerto Rico setView(lng = -65.795, lat = 18.316, zoom = 17) %>% # Add clickable markers for each collar location addCircleMarkers( lng = ~lng, lat = ~lat, popup = popup_info, radius = 8, color = "#ffffff", fillColor = "#2ec4b6", fillOpacity = 0.9, weight = 2, label = ~Collar # Hover tooltip showing Collar ID ) }) # --- SERVER LOGIC: COLLAR QUICK STATS --- selected_row <- reactive({ collar_stats %>% filter(Collar == input$selected_collar) }) output$collar_title <- renderUI({ span(paste("Profile for Collar:", input$selected_collar), style = "color: #2c3e50; font-weight: bold;") }) output$collar_metadata <- renderUI({ row <- selected_row() HTML(paste0( "Slope Position: ", tools::toTitleCase(row$Slope), "
", "Experimental Treatment: ", tools::toTitleCase(row$Treatment) )) }) output$collar_gas_stats <- renderUI({ row <- selected_row() HTML(paste0( "CO₂ Flux Mean: ", round(row$Mean_CO2Flux, 3), " ± ", round(row$SD_CO2Flux, 3), " μmol/m²/s
", "CH₄ Flux Mean: ", round(row$Mean_CH4Flux, 3), " ± ", round(row$SD_CH4Flux, 3), " nmol/m²/s
", "Soil Moisture Mean: ", round(row$Mean_SM, 3), " ± ", round(row$SD_SM, 3), " m3m-3
", "Soil Temperature Mean: ", round(row$Mean_ST, 3), " ± ", round(row$SD_ST, 3), " °C" )) }) # --- SERVER LOGIC: TREATMENT BAR CHARTS --- # --- GRAPH 1: Original Interactive Plot (Faceted by Slope) --- output$summary_bar_chart <- renderPlotly({ if (input$metric == "CO2") { y_mean <- "Mean_CO2Flux" y_sd <- "SD_CO2Flux" y_label <- "Mean CO2 Flux" plot_title <- "Mean CO2 Flux Across Soil Collars by Litter Treatment and Slope Position" } else { y_mean <- "Mean_CH4Flux" y_sd <- "SD_CH4Flux" y_label <- "Mean CH4 Flux" plot_title <- "Mean CH4 Flux Across Soil Collars by Litter Treatment and Slope Position" } p <- ggplot(collar_stats, aes(x = Collar, y = .data[[y_mean]], fill = Slope)) + geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = position_dodge(width = 0.9), color = "black", alpha = 0.8) + geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = .data[[y_mean]] - .data[[y_sd]], ymax = .data[[y_mean]] + .data[[y_sd]]), width = 0.2, position = position_dodge(width = 0.9)) + facet_wrap(~ Treatment, scales = "free_x") + labs(title = plot_title, x = "Collar ID", y = y_label, fill = "Collar Type (Slope)") + theme_minimal() + theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12), legend.position = "bottom") ggplotly(p) # Converts ggplot to interactive plotly }) # --- GRAPH 2: Significance Bar Chart --- # --- SERVER LOGIC: TREATMENT SIGNIFICANCE BAR CHART --- output$treatment_signif_chart <- renderPlot({ # 1. Dynamic setup based on selected metric if (input$metric == "CO2") { y_col <- "Mean_CO2Flux" y_label <- "Mean CO2 Flux" title_label <- "Mean CO2 Flux Grouped by Treatment" #2 comparisons for CO2 comp_list <- list(c("control", "green"), c("control", "senesced")) sig_annots <- c(control_vs_green_sig_co2, control_vs_senesced_sig_co2) y_positions <- c(4.8, 5.8) y_upper_lim <- 6.5 } else { y_col <- "Mean_CH4Flux" y_label <- "Mean CH4 Flux" title_label <- "Mean CH4 Flux Grouped by Treatment" #3 comparisons for CH4 comp_list <- list(c("control", "green"),c("control", "senesced"), c("control", "soil")) sig_annots <- c(control_vs_green_sig_ch4, control_vs_senesced_sig_ch4, control_vs_soil_sig_ch4) y_positions <- c(0.05, 0.18, 0.31) y_upper_lim <- 0.45 } # 2. Aggregate mean data by Treatment group treatment_summary <- collar_stats %>% group_by(Treatment) %>% summarise(Mean_Value = mean(.data[[y_col]], na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") # 3. Build the Plot (Moved 'annotations' outside of aes()) ggplot(treatment_summary, aes(x = Treatment, y = Mean_Value, fill = Treatment)) + geom_bar( stat = "identity", position = position_dodge(width = 0.9), color = "black", alpha = 0.85 ) + labs( title = title_label, x = "Treatment", y = y_label, fill = "Treatment" ) + #All comparisons in a single layer geom_signif( comparisons = comp_list, annotations = sig_annots, y_position = y_positions, tip_length = 0.03, vjust = -0.2 ) + theme_minimal() + theme( plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14), axis.text.x = element_text(size = 11), legend.position = "bottom" ) }) # --- SERVER LOGIC: TIMELINE EXPLORER (CONCEPT 1) --- # 1. Reactive filtered data based purely on chosen collars filtered_timeline_data <- reactive({ req(input$selected_timeline_collars) data <- alldays %>% filter(Collar %in% input$selected_timeline_collars) # Enforce chronological ordering along x-axis time_order <- c("pretreatment", "day1", "day2", "day3", "day4", "day5", "day6", "day7", "day8") data$Timepoint <- factor(data$Timepoint, levels = time_order) data }) # 2. TOP PLOT: Gas Flux Dynamic Plot by Collar output$timeline_gas_plot <- renderPlot({ df <- filtered_timeline_data() req(nrow(df) > 0) gas_col <- input$timeline_gas gas_label <- if (gas_col == "CO2Flux") "CO2 Flux (μmol/m²/s)" else "CH4 Flux (nmol/m²/s)" gas_title <- if (gas_col == "CO2Flux") "Soil CO2 Flux Trajectory by Collar" else "Soil CH4 Flux Trajectory by Collar" # Each chosen collar gets its own distinct color and clear line ggplot(df, aes(x = Timepoint, y = .data[[gas_col]], color = Collar, group = Collar)) + geom_line(linewidth = 1.2) + geom_point(size = 3) + labs( title = gas_title, x = NULL, # Kept blank so it shares the time axis with the bottom plot y = gas_label, color = "Collar ID" ) + theme_minimal() + theme( plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13), axis.text.x = element_blank(), axis.ticks.x = element_blank(), legend.position = "right" ) }) # 3. BOTTOM PLOT: Synchronized Abiotic Drivers (Soil Moisture & Temperature) output$timeline_abiotic_plot <- renderPlot({ df <- filtered_timeline_data() req(nrow(df) > 0) # Calculate group averages across selected collars per timepoint daily_abiotic <- df %>% group_by(Timepoint) %>% summarise( Mean_Moisture = mean(SoilMoisture, na.rm = TRUE), Mean_Temp = mean(SoilTemp, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop" ) # Rescale Soil Temperature (15–30°C) to match the Soil Moisture scale (0.1–0.5 m³/m³) temp_min <- 15; temp_max <- 30 moist_min <- 0.1; moist_max <- 0.5 scale_temp <- function(t) { moist_min + (t - temp_min) * (moist_max - moist_min) / (temp_max - temp_min) } unscale_temp <- function(m) { temp_min + (m - moist_min) * (temp_max - temp_min) / (moist_max - moist_min) } daily_abiotic <- daily_abiotic %>% mutate(Scaled_Temp = scale_temp(Mean_Temp)) ggplot(daily_abiotic, aes(x = Timepoint, group = 1)) + # Soil Moisture Ribbon & Line (Blue) geom_area(aes(y = Mean_Moisture), fill = "#2b8cbe", alpha = 0.25) + geom_line(aes(y = Mean_Moisture, color = "Soil Moisture"), linewidth = 1.2) + geom_point(aes(y = Mean_Moisture, color = "Soil Moisture"), size = 2.5) + # Soil Temperature Line (Orange/Red) geom_line(aes(y = Scaled_Temp, color = "Soil Temperature"), linewidth = 1.2, linetype = "dashed") + geom_point(aes(y = Scaled_Temp, color = "Soil Temperature"), size = 2.5) + # Secondary Y-axis for Temperature scale_y_continuous( name = "Soil Moisture (m³/m³)", sec.axis = sec_axis(~ unscale_temp(.), name = "Soil Temperature (°C)") ) + scale_color_manual( name = "Environmental Factor", values = c("Soil Moisture" = "#2b8cbe", "Soil Temperature" = "#e6550d") ) + labs( title = "Mean Soil Moisture and Soil Temperature Over Time", x = "Sampling Phase", y = "Soil Moisture (m³/m³)" ) + theme_minimal() + theme( plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13), axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 35, hjust = 1, size = 10), legend.position = "right" ) }) } # ------------------------------------------------------------------------- # 4. RUN APPLICATION # ------------------------------------------------------------------------- shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

```{r}
collar_stats <- left_join(collar_stats, sm_sd, by = "Collar")
```



Make graph of mean soil moisture
```{r}
ggplot(collar_stats, aes(x = Collar, y = sm_mean, fill = Slope)) +
  # 1. Bar Geometry
  geom_bar(
    stat = "identity",
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.9)
  ) +
  
  # 2. ADD THE ERROR BAR LAYER HERE
  # Use the Mean (collar_avgs) and the SD (SD_CO2) to define the range.
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(
      # The bottom of the error bar
      ymin = sm_mean - sm_sd,
      # The top of the error bar
      ymax = sm_mean + sm_sd
    ),
    # Adjust width to make caps visible
    width = 0.2,
    # Match the dodging (side-by-side positioning) of the bars
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.9)
  ) +
  
  # 3. Facets for Grouping
  facet_wrap(~ Treatment, scales = "free_x") +
  
  # 4. Labels and Themes
  labs(
    title = "Mean Soil Moisture Across Soil Collars by Litter Treatment and Slope Position",
    x = "Collar ID",
    y = "Mean Soil Moisture",
    fill = "Collar Type (Slope)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "bottom",
)
```

Finding Soil Temp Mean
```{r}
st_mean <- alldays %>%
  # 1. Group the data by the 'Collar' column
  group_by(Collar) %>%
  # 2. Calculate the mean CO2Flux for each group, ignoring missing values (NA)
  summarise(
    st_mean = mean(soil_temp, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

# Print the resulting table
print(st_mean)
```

Find Soil standard deviation
```{r}
st_sd <- alldays %>%
  # 1. Group the data by the 'Collar' column
  group_by(Collar) %>%
  # 2. Calculate the standard deviation of CO2Flux for each group
  summarise(
    st_sd = sd(soil_temp, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

# Print the resulting table
print(st_sd)
```


Add sd and mean of temp to data to collar_stats
```{r}
collar_stats <- left_join(collar_stats, st_mean, by = "Collar")

collar_stats <- left_join(collar_stats, st_sd, by = "Collar")
```
